Chapter 1

Jesus' Family Tree

1Alright — pull up. This right here is the bloodline of Jesus Christ. Son of David. Son of Abraham. I know, it's a list. Don't skip it. Every name in here is God keeping a promise he made centuries before anybody was ready for it. Original · Matthew 1:1The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.2Abraham had Isaac. Isaac had Jacob. Jacob had Judah and his brothers. Original · Matthew 1:2Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.3Judah had Perez and Zerah — and the mother was Tamar. Her story is messy. She's in the line anyway. Perez had Hezron. Hezron had Ram. Original · Matthew 1:3Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.4Ram had Amminadab. Amminadab had Nahshon. Nahshon had Salmon. Original · Matthew 1:4Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.5Salmon had Boaz — mother was Rahab. Boaz had Obed — mother was Ruth. Ruth wasn't even from Israel. Still made the list. Obed had Jesse. Original · Matthew 1:5Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.6Jesse had King David. And David had Solomon — by the woman who used to be Uriah's wife. Matthew doesn't even soften it. He leaves the scar right there in the record. Original · Matthew 1:6Jesse became the father of King David. David the king became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife.7Solomon had Rehoboam. Rehoboam had Abijah. Abijah had Asa. Original · Matthew 1:7Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.8Asa had Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat had Joram. Joram had Uzziah. Original · Matthew 1:8Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.9Uzziah had Jotham. Jotham had Ahaz. Ahaz had Hezekiah. Original · Matthew 1:9Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.10Hezekiah had Manasseh. Manasseh had Amon. Amon had Josiah. Some of these men were good. Some of them were terrible. The line runs straight through all of them. Original · Matthew 1:10Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.11Josiah had Jechoniah and his brothers — right as the whole nation got hauled off to Babylon. Everything falls apart. The list keeps going. Original · Matthew 1:11Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.12After Babylon: Jechoniah had Shealtiel. Shealtiel had Zerubbabel. Original · Matthew 1:12After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.13Zerubbabel had Abiud. Abiud had Eliakim. Eliakim had Azor. Original · Matthew 1:13Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.14Azor had Zadok. Zadok had Achim. Achim had Eliud. Original · Matthew 1:14Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.15Eliud had Eleazar. Eleazar had Matthan. Matthan had Jacob. Nobody famous left. The world's forgotten about this family. Original · Matthew 1:15Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.16And Jacob had Joseph, the husband of Mary. And Mary is the one who gave birth to Jesus — the one they call Christ. Catch the switch. Every other line said somebody had a son. This one doesn't. Original · Matthew 1:16Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.17So count it up. Fourteen generations from Abraham to David. Fourteen from David to Babylon. Fourteen from Babylon to the Christ. None of this was random. Original · Matthew 1:17So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.

How Jesus Was Born

18Now here's how the birth of Jesus Christ actually went down. His mother Mary was engaged to Joseph. And before they were ever together — she's pregnant. By the Holy Spirit. Original · Matthew 1:18Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.19Joseph is a good man. He's not about to drag her in front of the whole town and let them tear her apart. So he decides to end it quietly and carry the shame himself. Original · Matthew 1:19Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.20But he's up all night turning it over. And an angel of the Lord shows up in a dream and says, “Joseph, son of David, don't be afraid to take Mary as your wife. What has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. Original · Matthew 1:20But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.21She will give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus — because he is the one who will save his people from their sins.” Original · Matthew 1:21She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”22All of this happened to make good on what the Lord had said through the prophet: Original · Matthew 1:22Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,23“Look — the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel.” Which means: God with us. Original · Matthew 1:23“Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel,” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”24Joseph wakes up. Does exactly what the angel said. No argument, no stalling. He takes Mary home as his wife, Original · Matthew 1:24Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;25but he doesn't sleep with her until she's given birth to her firstborn son. And he named him Jesus. Original · Matthew 1:25and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.

Wise Men Follow a Star Across the World

1So Jesus is born in Bethlehem, down in Judea, back when Herod is king. And out of nowhere — wise men. From the east. They pull up in Jerusalem asking around, Original · Matthew 2:1Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,2“Where's the one who was born King of the Jews? We saw his star come up in the east. We came all this way to worship him.” Read that again. They crossed a desert on a hunch about a star. Original · Matthew 2:2“Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”3Herod hears the words born king and something in him goes cold. And the whole city feels it with him. When the man on the throne gets nervous, everybody gets nervous. Original · Matthew 2:3When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.4So he pulls in every chief priest and scribe he's got and asks them flat out: where is the Christ supposed to be born? Original · Matthew 2:4Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ would be born.5They don't even have to look it up. “Bethlehem. In Judea. The prophet wrote it: Original · Matthew 2:5They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,6‘You, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah — you are not the least of anything. Out of you is coming a ruler who will shepherd my people, Israel.'” Original · Matthew 2:6‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah; for out of you shall come a governor who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’ ”7So Herod pulls the wise men aside. Quiet. Just him and them. And he gets the exact timing of when that star first showed up. He's already doing math. Original · Matthew 2:7Then Herod secretly called the wise men, and learned from them exactly what time the star appeared.8Then he sends them to Bethlehem. “Go find the child. Look hard. And when you find him, come tell me — so I can go worship him too.” Every word of that was a lie. Original · Matthew 2:8He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”9They hear the king out and head off. And there it is again — that same star from the east. Out in front of them the whole way. Until it stops. Right over the place where the child was. Original · Matthew 2:9They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them until it came and stood over where the young child was.10And when they see that star stop, they lose it. Pure joy. All the way up. Original · Matthew 2:10When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.11They walk in the house and see the child with Mary his mother — and they hit the floor. Grown men with money and status, face down in front of a toddler. Then they open their treasures and hand it over: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Original · Matthew 2:11They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.12But God warns them in a dream — don't go back to Herod. So they take a whole different road home and Herod never sees them again. Original · Matthew 2:12Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.

Run. Get to Egypt.

13The second they're gone, an angel of the Lord shows up in Joseph's dream. “Get up. Take the child and his mother and get to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you. Herod is coming for this child to kill him.” Original · Matthew 2:13Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”14Joseph doesn't wait for sunrise. Gets up, gets the child and his mother, and they're gone. That same night. Headed for Egypt. Original · Matthew 2:14He arose and took the young child and his mother by night and departed into Egypt,15They stay down there until Herod dies. Which makes good on what the Lord said through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called my son.” Original · Matthew 2:15and was there until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

Herod Loses It

16When Herod figures out the wise men went around him, the rage takes over completely. He gives an order. Every boy in Bethlehem and the whole area around it — two years old and under — killed. He based the age on the timing the wise men gave him. That's what fear on a throne will do. Original · Matthew 2:16Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out and killed all the male children who were in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.17And that's when what Jeremiah the prophet said came true: Original · Matthew 2:17Then that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,18“A sound came out of Ramah. Weeping. Deep, tearing grief. Rachel crying over her children — and she would not be comforted, because they are gone.” Original · Matthew 2:18“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.”

Back Home to Nazareth

19Then Herod dies. And the angel of the Lord is back in Joseph's dream, down in Egypt. Original · Matthew 2:19But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,20“Get up. Take the child and his mother and go back to Israel. The ones who wanted him dead are dead.” Original · Matthew 2:20“Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the young child’s life are dead.”21So he gets up, takes the child and his mother, and heads back to Israel. Original · Matthew 2:21He arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.22Then he hears Archelaus is running Judea now — Herod's son, sitting in Herod's chair. Nope. Joseph's not walking his family back into that. God warns him in a dream, so he cuts up north into Galilee instead, Original · Matthew 2:22But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in the place of his father, Herod, he was afraid to go there. Original · Matthew 4:1Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.2Forty days. Forty nights. No food. Original · Matthew 4:2When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.3That's when the tempter slides in. Takes him into the holy city. Stands him up on the highest point of the temple. Everybody below looks like ants. Original · Matthew 4:5Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,6“If you're really the Son of God — jump. Original · Matthew 4:6and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’ ”7Jesus says, “It is also written: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'” Original · Matthew 4:7Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’ ”8One more try. He Didn't Come to Tear It Down

It Starts Way Before the Hands

Nothing Stays Hidden

16"Nobody lights a lamp and then covers it with a jar or shoves it under the bed. You put it on a stand, so anybody walking in can see. Original · Luke 8:16“No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.17Because nothing hidden is staying hidden. Original · Luke 8:17For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.18So pay attention to how you listen. Whoever has, gets more. And whoever doesn't have — even what he thinks he has gets taken." Original · Luke 8:18Be careful therefore how you hear. Chapter 1

In the Beginning Was the Word

1Before anything. Before time, before light, before the first thing was ever made — the Word already was. The Word was with God. And the Word was God. Original · John 1:1In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.2He was there with God in the beginning. From the very start. Original · John 1:2The same was in the beginning with God.3Everything that exists came into being through him. Nothing that has ever been made was made without him. Original · John 1:3All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.4Life was in him. And that life was the light of everyone. Original · John 1:4In him was life, and the life was the light of men.5The light shines in the dark. And the dark has never once put it out. Original · John 1:5The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.

John Comes to Point at the Light

6There was a man sent from God. His name was John. Original · John 1:6There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.7He came as a witness — to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him. Original · John 1:7The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.8He wasn’t the light himself. He came to point at it. Original · John 1:8He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.9The true light — the one that gives light to every person — was coming into the world. Original · John 1:9The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.10He was in the world. The world was made through him. And the world didn’t know him. Original · John 1:10He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.11He came to his own people. And his own people didn’t receive him. Original · John 1:11He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.12But everyone who did receive him — everyone who trusts his name — he gave them the right to become children of God. Original · John 1:12But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:13Not born of blood. Not born of what the body wants. Not born of anybody’s decision. Born of God. Original · John 1:13who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.14And the Word became flesh, and moved in among us. We saw his glory — the glory of the Father’s one and only Son — full of grace and truth. Original · John 1:14The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.15John sees him and can’t hold it in. He calls out, “This is the one I told you about. The one coming after me is ahead of me — because he was here before me.” Original · John 1:15John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’ ”16Out of everything he is, we have all received grace. And then more grace on top of that. Original · John 1:16From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.17The law came through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. Original · John 1:17For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.18Nobody has ever seen God. But the one and only Son, the one closest to the Father’s heart — he’s the one who showed us exactly who God is. Original · John 1:18No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.

John Tells Them Who He Isn’t

19So here’s John’s testimony. Jerusalem sends a whole delegation out to him — priests, Levites, official business — and they come with one question. “Who are you?” Original · John 1:19This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”20And John doesn’t dodge. Doesn’t even leave the door cracked. He says it flat: “I am not the Christ.” Original · John 1:20He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”21So they try again. “Okay — then Elijah?” “I’m not.” “The Prophet?” “No.” Man is giving them nothing. Original · John 1:21They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”22Now they’re stuck. “Then who are you? We have to bring something back to the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?” Original · John 1:22They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”23And John tells them, “I’m a voice. Philip and Nathanael Get Called

Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”44Philip was from Bethsaida — same hometown as Andrew and Peter. Joseph’s son.” Original · John 1:45Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses in the law and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”46Nathanael is not impressed. “Nazareth? Has anything good ever come out of Nazareth?” Philip doesn’t argue with him. He just says, “Come and see.” Original · John 1:46Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”47Jesus watches Nathanael walking up and says, out loud, “Now this is a real Israelite. Not a fake bone in him.” Original · John 1:47Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!”48Nathanael stops. “How do you know me?” Jesus tells him, “Before Philip ever called your name — when you were under the fig tree — I saw you.” Original · John 1:48Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”49And that does it. Something in Nathanael just folds. “Rabbi. You’re the Son of God. You’re the King of Israel.” Original · John 1:49Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! Chapter 3

Nicodemus Pulls Up at Night

1So there’s this Pharisee. Nicodemus. One of the Jewish leaders — a man with a reputation to protect. Original · John 3:1Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.2He comes to Jesus at night. Nobody around to see it. “Rabbi, we know you’re a teacher who came from God. Nobody could do the signs you’re doing unless God was with him.” Original · John 3:2He came to Jesus by night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.”3Jesus doesn’t do the small talk. He says, “I’m telling you the truth — unless someone is born again, they can’t even see God’s Kingdom.” Original · John 3:3Jesus answered him, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”4Nicodemus is lost. “Born? A grown man? He can’t climb back into his mother and start over.” Original · John 3:4Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?”5Jesus answers, “I’m telling you the truth — unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, they can’t enter God’s Kingdom. Original · John 3:5Jesus answered, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born of water and Spirit, he can’t enter into God’s Kingdom.6Flesh gives birth to flesh. The Spirit gives birth to spirit. Original · John 3:6That which is born of the flesh is flesh. That which is born of the Spirit is spirit.7Don’t be thrown that I told you, ‘You all have to be born again.’ Original · John 3:7Don’t marvel that I said to you, ‘You must all be born anew.’8The wind blows wherever it wants. You hear it — but you can’t tell where it came from or where it’s headed. That’s how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” Original · John 3:8The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”9Nicodemus goes, “How does any of this even work?” Original · John 3:9Nicodemus answered him, “How can these things be?”10Jesus says, “You’re Israel’s teacher, and this is where you get stuck? Original · John 3:10Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and don’t understand these things?11I’m telling you the truth: we speak about what we know, we testify to what we’ve seen — and you all still won’t take our word for it. Original · John 3:11Most certainly I tell you, we speak that which we know and testify of that which we have seen, and you don’t receive our witness.12If you can’t believe me about earthly things, how are you going to believe me about heavenly ones? Original · John 3:12If I told you earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?13Nobody has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven — the Son of Man. Original · John 3:13No one has ascended into heaven but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.14And the same way Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, the Son of Man has to be lifted up too, Original · John 3:14As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,15so that everyone who believes in him won’t perish, but will have eternal life. Original · John 3:15that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.16Because this is how much God loved the world: he gave his one and only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish, but have eternal life. Original · John 3:16For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.17God didn’t send his Son into the world to condemn it. He sent him so the world could be saved through him. Original · John 3:17For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.18Whoever believes in him isn’t condemned. Whoever doesn’t believe already stands condemned — because they refused to trust the name of God’s one and only Son. Original · John 3:18He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.19And here’s the verdict: the light came into the world. And people loved the dark better. Because what they were doing was evil. Original · John 3:19This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil.20Everybody doing wrong hates the light. Stays clear of it. Doesn’t want any of it exposed. Original · John 3:20For everyone who does evil hates the light and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.21But whoever lives in the truth walks straight into the light — so it’s plain to see that what they’ve done was done in God.” Original · John 3:21But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”

John Says: He Gets Bigger, I Get Smaller

22After this, Jesus and his disciples head out into the Judean countryside. He stays out there with them, baptizing. Original · John 3:22After these things, Jesus came with his disciples into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized.23John is baptizing too — over in Aenon near Salim, plenty of water out there. And people keep coming to get baptized. Original · John 3:23John also was baptizing in Enon near Salim, because there was much water there. They came and were baptized;24All of this is before John got thrown in prison. Original · John 3:24for John was not yet thrown into prison.25Then an argument kicks off between John’s disciples and a Jewish man about ceremonial washing. Original · John 3:25Therefore a dispute arose on the part of John’s disciples with some Jews about purification.26And it turns into this. Original · John 3:26They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, behold, he baptizes, and everyone is coming to him.”27John doesn’t flinch. “Nobody can receive anything unless heaven hands it to them. Original · John 3:27John answered, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven.28You heard me say it yourselves. I’m not the Christ. I was sent ahead of him. Original · John 3:28You yourselves testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before him.’29The bride belongs to the groom. The groom’s friend just stands there listening for his voice — and when he hears it, that’s the best moment of his whole night. That’s my joy. And it’s full. Original · John 3:29He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore my joy is made full.30He has to become greater. I have to become less. Original · John 3:30He must increase, but I must decrease.31The one who comes from above is over everything. Whoever comes from the earth belongs to the earth, and talks like it. The one who comes from heaven is over it all. Original · John 3:31“He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.32He testifies to what he has actually seen and heard — and hardly anybody takes his word for it. Original · John 3:32What he has seen and heard, of that he testifies; and no one receives his witness.33But whoever does take his word has put their stamp on it: God tells the truth. Original · John 3:33He who has received his witness has set his seal to this, that God is true.34The one God sent speaks God’s own words — because God gives him the Spirit without holding anything back. Original · John 3:34For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God gives the Spirit without measure.35The Father loves the Son and has put everything in his hands. Original · John 3:35The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.36Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever refuses the Son won’t see life — God’s wrath stays on him.” Original · John 3:36One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.”

Could this be the Christ?” Original · John 4:29“Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?”30So the whole town comes pouring out, headed straight for him. Original · John 4:30They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

The Fields Are Already Ready

31Meanwhile the disciples are still on him about food. “Rabbi. Eat something.” Original · John 4:31In the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”32He tells them, “I have food to eat that you don’t know anything about.” Original · John 4:32But he said to them, “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”33And they’re looking at each other like — did somebody bring him a plate? Original · John 4:33The disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?”34Jesus says, “My food is doing what the one who sent me wants, and finishing his work. Original · John 4:36He who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit to eternal life, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.37The old saying holds up: one plants, another harvests. Original · John 4:37For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’38I sent you to harvest a field you never worked. Other people did the labor. 43After those two days he moves on into Galilee. Original · John 4:45So when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.46So he’s back in Cana of Galilee — same place he turned the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.47The second he hears Jesus is back from Judea, he goes to him and begs him to come down and heal his son. The boy is dying. Original · John 4:47When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.48Jesus tells him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you just won’t believe.” Original · John 4:48Jesus therefore said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.”49And the man doesn’t argue about it. He just says, “Sir. Please. Come down before my little boy dies.” Original · John 4:49The nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”50Jesus tells him, “Go on home. Your son lives.” And the man takes him at his word. Turns around and goes. Original · John 4:50Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.51He’s still on the road when his servants come running up with the news. “Your boy is alive.” Original · John 4:51As he was going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!”52He asks them what time he turned the corner. They tell him, “The fever broke yesterday. One in the afternoon.” Original · John 4:52So he inquired of them the hour when he began to get better. Done after he came out of Judea into Galilee. Original · John 4:54This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee.

Chapter 5

Thirty-Eight Years at the Pool

1A while later there’s a Jewish feast, so Jesus goes up to Jerusalem. Original · John 5:1After these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.2Now in Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there’s a pool. Bethesda, they call it in Hebrew. Five covered porches. Original · John 5:2Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.3And those porches are packed. Sick people laid out everywhere — blind, unable to walk, paralyzed — all of them waiting on the water to move. Original · John 5:3In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water;4Because every so often an angel would come down and stir the water, and the first one in after that got healed of whatever they had. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.”11He tells them, “The man who healed me is the one who said, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’” Original · John 5:11He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your mat and walk.’ ”12So they go, “Who? Who told you to pick it up and walk?” Original · John 5:12Then they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat and walk’?”13And he had no idea. Original · John 5:15The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.

The Son Does What He Sees the Father Doing

16And that’s when they start coming after Jesus. Because he was doing this on the Sabbath. Original · John 5:16For this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath.17But Jesus tells them, “My Father is still working. A time is coming when everyone in the graves will hear his voice Original · John 5:28Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice29and come out. Everything Points Back to Him

Original · John 17:3This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.4I glorified you here on earth. The work you gave me — I finished it. Original · John 17:4I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.5So now, Father, glorify me in your own presence, with the glory I had with you before the world existed. I have kept those whom you have given me. None of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.13Now I’m coming to you. Jesus in Front of Annas

12So the soldiers, the commander, and the officers grab Jesus and tie him up. Original · John 18:12So the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him,13They march him to Annas first. The Crucifixion

They Lay Him in the Tomb

38After this, Joseph of Arimathea steps up. He’d been a disciple of Jesus — quietly, because he was scared of the leaders. But not today. He goes to Pilate and asks for the body. Pilate says yes. So he comes and takes him. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.42It was the Preparation Day, and the tomb was close. So that’s where they laid Jesus. Chapter 20

The Tomb Is Empty

1First day of the week. Early. Still dark out. Mary Magdalene goes to the tomb — and the stone is gone. Rolled away. Original · John 20:1Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.2So she runs. Straight to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one Jesus loved. “They’ve taken the Lord out of the tomb and we don’t know where they put him!” Original · John 20:2Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”3And those two are out the door. Headed for the tomb. Original · John 20:3Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb.4Both of them running. Full sprint. And the other disciple is faster — he leaves Peter behind and gets there first. Original · John 20:4They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first.5He bends down, looks in. The linen cloths are lying right there. But he doesn’t go in. Original · John 20:5Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; yet he didn’t enter in.6Then Peter comes up behind him — and Peter does not stop at the entrance. Walks straight in.
